messages.content: You are the Chief Architecture Advisor for EvolvixOS. Review this phase, provide a score (1-10), identify issues by severity, and recommend next steps.

PHASE 117 IMPLEMENTATION REPORT: Integration and Stability

## Summary
Fixed all critical infrastructure issues: AI Gateway 404, Nginx route misalignment, customer-success port conflict, RBAC auth middleware, and test file consolidation. All 12 production endpoints now returning 200.

## Issues Fixed

### 1. AI Gateway 404 (Critical)
- Root cause: Nginx proxy_pass pointing to port 3500 instead of actual port 3400
- Fix: Corrected proxy_pass to http://localhost:3400/
- Result: /ai-gateway/health → 200, /ai-gateway/invoke → 405 (correct for GET, needs POST)

### 2. Nginx Route Misalignment (Critical)
- Root cause: Multiple services had wrong proxy_pass ports or incorrect prefix stripping
- Fixed routes: /queue/agent/stats (4300), /monitoring/health (3700), /agents/agents (3600), /core-agents/agents (4000), /agent-exec/health (4100), /sandbox/health (4200), /orchestration/health (3800)
- All 12 tested endpoints now return 200

### 3. Customer Success Port Conflict (High)
- Root cause: Customer-success container mapped to port 3400, conflicting with AI Gateway (host network on 3400)
- Fix: Moved customer-success to port 3300 with correct image (app.main:app instead of engine:app)
- Result: /support/health → 200

### 4. RBAC Auth Middleware (High)
- Built RBACMiddleware (BaseHTTPMiddleware) with:
  - Route-to-permission mapping (14 route prefixes → RBAC resource:action)
  - Method-to-action mapping (GET→read, POST→write, PATCH→write, DELETE→delete)
  - Public routes bypass (11 routes including /health, /docs, /openapi.json)
  - Backwards compatible (allows access when no X-User-ID header present)
  - Permission denied returns 403 with resource:action info
  - Response headers include X-RBAC-Resource, X-RBAC-Action, X-RBAC-User
- require_permission() decorator for per-endpoint protection
- 11 middleware tests
- RBAC container upgraded to v1.1.0 with /middleware-config endpoint

### 5. Test Consolidation (Medium)
- Removed 7 duplicate queue API test files (test_queue_api.py through test_queue_api_v34.py)
- Consolidated from 30 to 23 test files
- Kept only test_queue_api_v35.py (latest version)
- All tests still passing

### 6. RBAC Duplicate System Roles Fix (Critical from Phase 116)
- Root cause: ON CONFLICT clause didn't handle NULL org_id (PostgreSQL treats NULL != NULL)
- Fix: Changed to WHERE NOT EXISTS approach for seeding system roles
- Deleted 6 duplicate system roles from production PG
- Created unique index with COALESCE for NULL org_id handling
- Result: 7 roles total (6 system + 1 custom), no duplicates

## Production Verification
All 12 endpoints returning 200 via https://evolvixos.com:
- / → 200 (frontend)
- /ai-gateway/health → 200
- /queue/agent/stats → 200
- /monitoring/health → 200
- /agents/agents → 200
- /support/health → 200
- /rbac/dashboard → 200
- /enterprise/dashboard → 200
- /core-agents/agents → 200
- /agent-exec/health → 200
- /sandbox/health → 200
- /orchestration/health → 200

## Test Results
- 615 total tests passed, 7 skipped (up from 604)
- 23 test files (down from 30)
- 26 Docker containers running
- RBAC v1.1.0 with auth middleware
- 14 protected route prefixes, 11 public routes

## Platform State
- 836+ total tests (615 Python + 232 Rust, some Python tests not counted due to consolidation)
- 26 containers
- 23 PG tables
- 67 Python modules + 7 Rust pallets
- All endpoints accessible via https://evolvixos.com
- Blockchain at block #18,544+

## Questions for GPT-4o
1. Is the RBAC middleware approach correct (backwards compatible, fail-open)?
2. Should we enforce RBAC on all endpoints now (break backwards compatibility)?
3. What should Phase 118 be: Smart Contract Platform (as per the roadmap)?
4. Any remaining stability issues to address?
